title: What print does, what return does
idea: TOOL: print writes to the screen and gives the code nothing back; return gives a value to the code but writes nothing to the screen.

exercises.prompt:
Look:

def show_double(n):
    print(n * 2)

When you call show_double(5), what happens?
options: the code receives the value 10 to use
exercises.explanation: print(n * 2) writes 10 to the screen. It SHOWS the answer. It does not hand anything back to the code.

exercises.prompt:
Look:

def give_double(n):
    return n * 2

When you call give_double(5), what happens?
options: the value 10 is handed back to the code; nothing appears on screen
exercises.explanation: return n * 2 hands 10 back to whoever called it. By itself it prints NOTHING. If you want to see it, the caller must print it.

exercises.prompt: print puts something on the screen; return does not put anything on the screen.
exercises.explanation: Exactly. print is the only one of the two that writes to the screen. return quietly hands a value back to the code.

exercises.prompt: return hands a value back to the code; print does not hand a value back to the code.
exercises.explanation: Right. return is the only one that gives the code a value to keep using. print just displays and gives the code nothing useful back.

exercises.prompt: Match each line to what it does.

pairs.right: writes the answer on the screen
hands the answer back to the code

exercises.explanation: Same arithmetic, two different destinations: the screen (print) versus the calling code (return).

exercises.prompt: A friend says 'return shows the answer on the screen.' Are they right?
options: No - return hands it to the code; it shows nothing by itself
Yes, but only for big numbers
exercises.explanation: This is the classic mix-up. return is silent on screen. To SEE a returned value, the caller has to print it.

exercises.prompt: You want the code to keep using a sub-plan's answer later. Which line belongs in the sub-plan?
exercises.explanation: return answer gives the value to the code. print(answer) would only show it and leave the code empty-handed.

exercises.prompt:
Look:

def add(a, b):
    return a + b

You run add(3, 4) on its own line. What appears on the screen?
exercises.explanation: The value 7 is handed back, but no one printed it, so the screen stays blank. Returning is not the same as showing.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: print was the very first tool you learned, and it still just shows things on the screen.
exercises.explanation: Yes - print has done the same job since Unit 1: display a value. Nothing about sub-plans changes that.

exercises.prompt: In one sentence, the difference is...
options: print talks to the screen; return talks to the code
they are two names for the same thing
exercises.explanation: Screen vs code. That is the whole distinction, and remembering it prevents the most common sub-plan bug.
